text:
I loved the blue ardently:

the exalted mountains, the subtle

sapphire crêpes of the firmament,

the endless sea, whose lament

cradled my youthful dreams.


My lute fell silent when each pure star

unfurled its bud,

the universe sailed in stillness,

and the moon, a silver sickle, rose and reaped

the sheaf of the night’s thick shadows.


I sang when dawn drew back

its rosy veils in the East,

when the dew descended upon the fields,

and the sun, a golden urn opening,

flooded all the heavens with light.


But today I love the night, the graceful one,

of sweet majesty, tranquil

and solemn hours, the sovereign Nubian,

the one of splendid American pomp:

the tropical night of your pupils!


Today I evade the blushes of dawn;

its golden arrow wounds me,

and the heart, without sorrow or anger,

dilates only before the blackness of your eyes,

like the iris of an owl.


What enchantment could equal yours,

O my night? Your beauty astonishes me!

I, who flee the splendors of morning,

let my soul flutter, like a firefly,

its sparkling wings in your shadow!


If I must always feel that gaze

fixed upon my face, powerful and tender,

farewell forever, blond dawn!

maiden in rose-colored dress:

may eternal night reign around me!


O night! Come to me, full of enchantment;

while you advance on mysterious wings,

my song will be for you alone,

and in the brown folds of your mantle,

my hopes will open their cups!

translation.title: I Loved the Blue Ardently
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem’s conversion from daylight to the beloved’s tropical night, including the moon’s sickle, owl’s iris, and firefly imagery.
